title: SLO Telemetry Calibration and Capacity Feedback Runbook
author: Asha Nair
content:
Summary

This runbook defines the standard process for calibrating SLO telemetry signals (latency and availability) and for feeding those calibrated signals into capacity planning and automated mitigation systems. It covers the measurement baseline, normalization techniques for multi-region/multi-quantization servings, automated backfill for missing telemetry, and the feedback loop that converts SLO consumption signals into capacity adjustments and stakeholder notifications.

Goals

- Ensure SLO telemetry reflects real customer experience across variants (quantized models, shard configurations, dedicated vs host).
- Reduce false-positive SLO breaches caused by noisy telemetry or telemetry gaps.
- Feed accurate error budget burn signals into capacity autoscaling and oncall escalation tooling.
- Maintain a reproducible audit trail for SLO adjustments and capacity decisions.

Scope

Applies to production inference services and the following SLOs: request p50/p95/p99 latency, request success rate (2xx), stream stability (no mid-stream disconnects), and embedding completion rate. This runbook does NOT apply to offline batch evaluation telemetry (see evaluation-runbooks).

Owners and Roles

- Primary owner: eng-sre-runtime (oncall rota lead)
- Secondary owner: eng-serving-runtime (kernel & quantization SME)
- Stakeholders: product-ml, customer-success (for enterprise tenants), infra-costs
- Approver for SLO changes: SRE director + product-ml manager

When to run this procedure

1) Quarterly SLO recalibration (scheduled)
2) After onboarding of a new model variant or quantization profile
3) Following a deployment that changes latency characteristics (e.g., new kernel, allocator change, NVLink change)
4) Immediately after detecting a sustained unexplained SLO drift for >= 1 hour

Signals and Data Sources

- Primary telemetry: request_trace_latency_ms, request_http_status, stream_disconnect_count, kvcache_hit_ratio
- Derived signals: normalized_request_latency, tenant_weighted_error_budget_burn
- Secondary sources: synthetic canary results, platform-level GPU utilization metrics, infra autoscaler events, cloud-region CPU/network metrics
- Storage: long-term raw traces in telemetry-retention (7d hot, 90d warm), aggregated SLO rollups in slo-rollups (30d hot), canary archives in canary-store

Normalization and Calibration Methodology

1) Apply service-level filters: remove healthcheck endpoints, internal control-plane calls, and debug-only routes.
2) Group by serving path, model_variant, quantization_flag, and region.
3) For latency metrics: compute p50/p95/p99 per-group using trace-level histograms (do NOT approximate with means).
4) Correct for sample bias: if synthetic-canary:production ratio < 0.05 for a group, mark group as low-sample and increase uncertainty band in dashboards.
5) Cross-variant baseline: for new quantized variants, compute delta_vs_baseline = p95_quantized - p95_fp16 over a 72h window; if delta > configured threshold (see thresholds table) trigger performance review.

Thresholds and Default Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Rationale | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---|
| p95 latency delta trigger | 25 ms | Practical user threshold for UI snappiness | eng-serving-runtime |
| low-sample ratio threshold | 0.05 | Below this synthetic coverage we flag uncertainty | eng-sre-runtime |
| missing-telemetry tolerance | 5 minutes | If aggregated rollup hasn't updated, trigger backfill pipeline | eng-sre-runtime |
| auto-adjust capacity burn rate window | 30 minutes | Smoothing window for autoscaler input | eng-sre |

Automated Backfill Procedure (missing telemetry)

1) Detection: telemetry-orchestrator raises a MissingRollup event when slo-rollups has not updated for a service-group for >= missing-telemetry tolerance.
2) Fast-path: attempt re-ingest from telemetry-retention hot store using backfill CLI:

   backfill-slo-rollup --service my-service --group "model=redwood-small,region=us-west-2" --from "now-2h" --to "now"

3) If hot-store reingest fails, fall back to warm-store rehydrate (this takes longer; estimate 30–90m).
4) Post-backfill validation: run ./validate-slo-rollup --service my-service --group <group> and ensure p95/p99 are within +/-5% of pre-gap baseline.
5) If validation fails, escalate to eng-sre-runtime with evidence bundle (see Evidence Collection).

SLO-to-Capacity Feedback Loop (automated)

Inputs:
- tenant_weighted_error_budget_burn (1m window)
- normalized_request_latency p95 drift (30m smoothed)
- infra_utilization[GPU/CPU/NET] 5m

Decision logic (simplified):
1) If error_budget_burn > 0.6 for 30m AND infra_utilization < 70% then: trigger targeted capacity increase for affected model_variant with max burst = 20% of current pool.
2) If p95 drift > p95 latency delta trigger AND GPU util > 75% for 15m: open urgent capacity review (human-in-loop) and prevent automated scale-down for 1h.
3) If sudden full-tenant error burn spike (>0.8) across multiple regions: engage cross-region fallback policy and notify oncall.

Automation implementation notes:
- Autoscaler reads a calibrated signal: capacity_input_score = clamp( normalized_burn * variant_weight * (1 + infra_pressure_factor), 0 , 1.5)
- All automated actions are recorded to capacity-audit-log with a trace id.
- Automated scale-up actions create a temporary priority ticket in provisioning-queue with TTL 4h; if ticket not confirmed by humans, system will attempt graceful scale-down after TTL.

Evidence Collection for Escalation

When telemetry calibration or backfill fails or an automated adjustment is contested, collect:
- slo-rollup snapshots (pre-gap and post-gap) in JSON
- raw traces for 15m window surrounding incident (trace IDs)
- canary-snapshots and synthetic-run results
- autoscaler decision logs (capacity-audit-log id)
- related deployment/change event from deploy-log (commit SHA, rollout ID)

Validation and Post-action Checks

After any manual or automated capacity action, run the following checks within 30 minutes:
1) verify slo-rollups updated and p95/p99 moved toward target if capacity increase was applied
2) confirm no regressions in stream stability or error rate
3) check infra metrics to ensure no resource saturation (GPU memory, PCIe errors)
4) update incident / change ticket with result and attach evidence bundle

Change Control and Approval Process

- Non-urgent SLO target changes require: SRE owner proposal -> stakeholder review (product-ml + customer-success) -> SRE director approval.
- Urgent temporary SLO relaxations (mitigation window <= 72h) may be approved by oncall lead and must be ratified within 5 business days.
- Permanent SLO adjustments must include retrospective with synthetic canary baselines and cost impact estimate.

Runbook: Step-by-step Play (example: new quantized variant rollout)

1) Pre-rollout (eng-serving-runtime): create canary config with 5% traffic, enable synthetic canaries for 24h, and create calibration job:

   create-canary --service my-service --variant q4_0 --traffic 0.05 --synthetic-profile default-latency
   start-calibration-job --group "model=my-service,variant=q4_0,region=us-west-2" --duration 24h

2) Calibration job collects p95 deltas against baseline and writes results to canary-store. If delta <= p95 latency delta trigger -> proceed. If delta > trigger -> abort and open performance-review.
3) Post-rollout (0–72h): monitor tenant-weighted-error_budget_burn and normalized_request_latency. If burn > 0.5 sustained for 30m, automatically reduce variant traffic by 50% and notify stakeholders.

Rollback and Safety Procedures

- Automated rollback is allowed if performance-review flag is set and failure criteria met (p95 delta > 100ms or success rate < 98% for 10m).
- Manual rollback steps: pin traffic to previous variant, initiate canary to validate baseline, then fully roll back through orchestrator.

Dashboards and Alerts

- Dashboards: SLO Calibration Overview (per-service), Variant Delta Explorer, Capacity Feedback Monitor.
- Alerts: Missing-rollup (P1), Delta-exceeds-threshold (P2), Auto-adjust-action-failed (P1), Backfill-failure (P2).

Verification Checklist (pre-check before approving automated capacity actions)

- [ ] rollup data is recent (<= 5m)
- [ ] synthetic canary healthy for last 30m
- [ ] infra utilization checked and below emergency thresholds
- [ ] evidence bundle created and attached to action

Audit and Postmortem Guidance

- All automated capacity decisions must remain in capacity-audit-log for 1 year.
- Postmortem for any contested automated action must include the calibration job output, autoscaler input signals, and the human approval trail.

Appendices

A. Useful commands
- backfill-slo-rollup --service <svc> --group "<group>" --from <ts> --to <ts>
- validate-slo-rollup --service <svc> --group <group>
- show-capacity-audit --trace-id <id>

B. Contact list

- eng-serving-runtime cadence owners: runtime-leads@redwood.com
